# CORI Line Chart Template

A checklist of every code chunk needed to produce a standard CORI line chart
using `theme_cori_precise`. Sections marked **[optional]** are situational.

---

## 1. Libraries

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(cori.charts)
library(ragg)
library(svglite)

load_fonts()
```

---

## 2. Data prep

Your chart-specific data wrangling. Output should be a tidy data frame
(`chart_dta`) with one row per line per x-value.

**Required columns:**
- x column (e.g. `year`, or a `Date`)
- y column (e.g. `avg_pci_index`, `value`)
- category/group column (e.g. `category`) — used for color and line labels

---

## 3. Build the figure

```r
fig <- chart_dta %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, color = category, group = category)) +

  # [optional] Dashed baseline for indexed charts (e.g. indexed to 100%)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "white", linewidth = 1) +       # hides solid gridline at baseline
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed",   # draws dashed baseline
             color = "#d0d2ce") +

  # [optional] Shaded annotation period (e.g. recession, COVID)
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = 2007, xmax = 2009,    # adjust to your period
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,     # or use data-specific y limits
           fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5) +

  # Chart lines
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +

  # Y axis — adjust limits, labels, and breaks to your data
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
    limits = c(NA, NA),                              # set explicit limits if needed
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)     # or label_number(), label_dollar(), etc.
  ) +

  # X axis — set inside set_chart_limits() below; only add labels/breaks here
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 1, big.mark = ""),
    n.breaks = 5
  ) +

  # Colors — match values to your category column
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Category A" = "#00835D",
    "Category B" = "#211448",
    "Category C" = "#808080"
  )) +

  # Theme — always include; type can be "line", "bar", "scatter", "map"
  theme_cori_precise(type = "line") +

  # Per-chart overrides — margin and legend are the most common
  theme(
    plot.margin    = margin(13, 60, 13, 13, "pt"),   # increase right (2nd value) if labels clip
    legend.position = "none"                          # remove if using a legend instead of labels
  ) +

  # Direct line labels — replace with legend if lines are too close to label
  label_lines(
    data       = chart_dta,
    x_col      = year,
    y_col      = value,
    label_col  = category,
    color_col  = category,      # remove if you want black labels
    min_gap    = 0.05,          # in data units; increase if labels overlap
    label_width = 12            # auto-wrap labels at this width (set to Inf to disable)
  ) +

  # Titles
  labs(
    title    = "Title goes here",
    subtitle = "Y-axis description goes here (italic, acts as y-axis label)",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = NULL,
    caption  = "Source: ..."
  ) +

  # Gridline truncation — always include for line charts; keeps grid from overshooting data
  set_chart_limits(chart_dta, x_col = year)
```

---

## 4. Export

```r
# Produces both PNG and SVG at report width (6.5") by default
save_chart(fig, "export/my_chart_name", preset = "report")

# For PowerPoint slides (4.75" wide)
save_chart(fig, "export/my_chart_name", preset = "slide")

# PNG only, no logo
save_chart(fig, "export/my_chart_name", preset = "report",
           formats = "png", add_logo = FALSE)

# Custom aspect ratio (default is 0.625; taller = higher value)
save_chart(fig, "export/my_chart_name", preset = "report", aspect_ratio = 0.75)
```

---

## Optional overrides for one-off adjustments

Only use these when the baked-in defaults don't work for a specific chart.
Add a custom `spec` object and pass it to all three functions:

```r
spec <- cori_chart_spec(
  font_title    = 11,   # pt
  font_subtitle = 9,
  font_axis     = 8,
  font_label    = 9,
  font_caption  = 8,
  font_legend   = 9,
  tick_length   = 4,    # pt
  gridline_width = 0.25 # mm
)

fig + theme_cori_precise(type = "line", spec = spec)
     label_lines(..., spec = spec)
save_chart(fig, "export/my_chart", preset = "report", spec = spec)
```

---

## Quick reference: what lives where

| Decision | Where to change it |
|---|---|
| Font sizes (all charts) | `cori_chart_spec()` defaults in `theme_cori_precise.R` |
| Canvas width | `cori_chart_spec()` `width_report` / `width_slide` |
| Tick length, gridline weight | `cori_chart_spec()` defaults |
| Line colors | `scale_color_manual()` in chart script |
| Line stroke width | `geom_line(linewidth = ...)` in chart script |
| Label spacing | `label_lines(min_gap = ...)` in chart script |
| Label wrapping | `label_lines(label_width = ...)` in chart script |
| Right margin (label clipping) | `theme(plot.margin = ...)` in chart script |
| Aspect ratio for one chart | `save_chart(aspect_ratio = ...)` |
| Y axis scale / breaks | `scale_y_continuous()` in chart script |
